lines.text: Lesson twelve: margin and leverage. Why small price moves can feel very big.
Two traders each put 100 USDT into the same BTC futures trade.
BTC rises 2%. Trader A gains 2 USDT. Trader B gains 20 USDT.
Then BTC falls to 2% below the start. A loses 2. B loses 20.
Same coin, same move. What made the difference? Leverage.
First word: margin. Initial margin is the money you set aside to open a futures position.
Your futures wallet holds 500 USDT. You lock 100 USDT as margin. 400 stays free.
Think of a deposit on a rented car. Any damage comes out of that deposit.
Next: notional exposure. That's the full value of the position, in USDT.
With 100 USDT of margin, you could hold a position worth 1,000 USDT.
Price moves act on the full 1,000 USDT, not just on your 100.
Leverage is how many times bigger the position is than your margin.
At 1x, 100 USDT of margin holds 100 of notional. At 3x, 300. At 10x, 1,000.
So notional is roughly margin times leverage. Your 100 USDT does not change.
Leverage is like a magnifying glass. It enlarges every move, good and bad.
Now one price path, three ways. Each trader is long with 100 USDT of margin.
BTC rises 2%, to 61,200. 1x makes 2 USDT. 3x makes 6. 10x makes 20.
Then it falls to 58,800, 2% below the start. Now 1x loses 2, 3x loses 6, 10x loses 20.
The market moved the same for all three. Leverage only changed the size of the result.
A worked example. Gross PnL is about notional times the signed percentage move.
1,000 USDT times minus 2% is minus 20 USDT, before fees and funding.
Divide by your margin: minus 20 over 100 is minus 20%.
A 2% price move became 20% of your money.
This works in both directions. Say BTC falls 10%.
At 1x, you lose 10 USDT, 10% of your margin. At 10x, you lose 100 USDT: all of it, on paper.
In reality, the exchange closes the position before that point. That's liquidation.
Where exactly depends on its rules and costs.
Maintenance margin is the minimum the exchange needs to keep your position open.
Your margin balance is your margin plus any open profit or loss. Losses push it down.
Fall to the maintenance level, and the exchange can close the position. Its rules set the level.
You also choose a margin mode: isolated or cross.
Isolated: losses on that position generally stay within the margin you gave it.
Like a separate envelope of cash. The other 400 USDT is not touched by it.
Cross: your whole futures balance backs your positions. One loss can reach far more.
Neither mode is safe. They decide how far a loss can reach.
A common mistake: thinking leverage is free extra money.
It isn't. It's extra exposure. Losses on the full 1,000 come out of your 100.
And no leverage number is safe. Lower leverage only means smaller swings.
Your turn. Margin 50 USDT, 5x, long. BTC rises 4%. Find the notional, the PnL and the % of margin.
Notional: 50 times 5 is 250 USDT. PnL: 250 times 4% is plus 10 USDT.
That's 20% of your margin. Had BTC fallen 4%, it would be minus 10 USDT.
Did you get it? Well done.
Before you go further, know the risks.
Leverage magnifies losses just as much as gains.
If losses eat your margin, the exchange can close your position. More on that next lesson.
Fees and funding are charged on the notional, so they grow with leverage.
There is no safe leverage. And you can always choose WAIT, or no trade.
Let's recap.
Notional is about margin times leverage.
Gross PnL is about notional times the signed move, before fees.
Leverage magnifies gains and losses alike. No leverage is safe.
Check yourself: 100 USDT of margin at 10x. BTC falls 3%. What's the PnL?
Minus 30 USDT, which is 30% of your margin.
Next up, T13: liquidation, funding and futures risks. See you there!
